messages:
amelia: heads-up — support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting huge latency and 429s for US customers starting ~09:12 UTC. They say requests are routing to eu-west-1 even though their org is pinned to us-east-1. ticket: INC-8421

sofia: linking the ticket and logs — https://support.internal/INC-8421 :eyes:

lisa-cs: customer provided curl repro. Looks simple:
```
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxxx' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east-1' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They see 200 quickly sometimes but mostly 500/429 and p50 latency jumps from 80ms -> 700ms.

devon: observed same spike on ingress metrics at 09:11 UTC: sudden increase in cross-region egress from us-east nodes to eu-west pools. Investigating routing service.

ops-bot: Incident created: routing-fallback-high-latency-1950012345 by amelia

kai: quick check: routing service change pushed at 09:05 UTC by infra team — policy TTL defaults lowered from 300s -> 30s in the last rollout (infra/route-ttl-pr #452). Could be related.

sofia: that's suspicious. If affinity TTL is too short, requests might lose sticky routing and then fallback picks eu variant under load. Any config diff?

devon: grabbing control-plane logs for that window. snippet: 
```
[09:10:58] route-eval user=acme org=acme-prod pref=us-east-1 affinity_ttl=30 -> route: eu-west-1 reason=fallback_capacity
[09:11:02] proxy: upstream eu-west-1 backend selected, latency=680ms
[09:11:05] auth: token validated, account=acme, billing_unit=client-123
```
Not seeing auth failures. Route decision indicates fallback due to capacity but affinity shows short TTL.

james-eng: capacity alarm was triggered in us-east at 09:08 (autoscale hiccup), but there was still available capacity. Why would policy mark fallback_capacity? Possibly mis-evaluated available capacity because of stale capacity cache TTL mismatch.

amelia: customer escalated to Priority 1 due to production impact, requesting rollback or mitigation. Any quick patch we can do to force region affinity back to us-east for this org?

devon: we can push a per-org override: set route_affinity_override[acme-prod]=us-east-1 and affinity_ttl=600. Doing a canary in prod now (09:20).

ops-bot: Deploy started: route-affinity-override-acme (deploy id dpl-778).

kai: also noticing billing events: duplicate billing events for some retries — looks like client retries + fallback caused double counting. I'll open a billing ticket in parallel.

lisa-cs: customer wants repro steps so they can validate when we fix. Recommend they use the header `X-Region` and `X-Request-Id` and capture response `server-region` header. Ask them to run 3-5 requests and paste response headers.

devon: can confirm override pushed at 09:22 UTC, probes show subsequent requests landing on us-east within 30s, latency back to normal. Patch reverted global TTL change at 09:30.

sofia: post-action notes: root cause appears to be a combination of two changes — (1) global affinity TTL reduced to 30s in infra rollout, (2) capacity cache staleness that underreported available us-east capacity under a short spike, causing fallback decisions to choose eu-west. The short TTL increased churn so more requests hit fallback while cache had brief inconsistency.

james-eng: mitigation performed: per-org override for affected customers + rollback of TTL change. Long-term: add a grace period to fallback decision (hold for N sec) and add cache coherence check during low-latency fallback decisions.

amelia: customer confirmed at 09:35 UTC that errors stopped and latencies normalized. Provided them timeline and will follow up with RCA.

lisa-cs: notes for support follow-up: explain we rolled back TTL change, applied temporary override, fixed double-billing edge (billing team to credit any duplicate charges), and will share postmortem with customers by EOD.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: routing-fallback-high-latency-1950012345 at 09:36 UTC.

sofia: adding repro snippet for future tests — run 100 short requests with header `X-Client-Region` and check `server-region` header distribution. Quick script: 
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxxx' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep server-region; done | sort | uniq -c
```

amelia: next steps: draft RCA, coordinate credits with billing, add test to canary pipeline to detect affinity TTL regressions. Assigning action items to infra/route and billing.

lisa-cs: thanks everyone — customer appreciated the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
